# Jubilees Chapter 32 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob at Bethel; Levi's priestly investment; the tithing law

---

**32:1** And at that night at Bethel an angel of the LORD appeared to Jacob and said: "I am the God of Bethel, where thou didst anoint the pillar and where thou didst vow a vow to me. Arise therefore and go from this land and return to the land of thy nativity."

**32:2** And Jacob arose early and summoned his wives and his children and all that was his, and they went up and arrived at Bethel.

**32:3** And Jacob burned an offering at Bethel on the altar which he had built, and he tithed all that came with him.

**32:4** And it came to pass that in those days Levi had a dream, and the angels of the LORD descended and they appointed him to be a priest, and to serve before the LORD.

**32:5** And Jacob awoke from his sleep and blessed the LORD.

**32:6** And he had Jacob count all the things that he had, and he began to count from his elder sons. Reuben was first, Simeon second, Levi third, Judah fourth, Dan fifth, Naphtali sixth, Gad seventh, Asher eighth, Issachar ninth, Zebulun tenth, Joseph eleventh, Benjamin twelfth.

**32:7** And he began anew to count them, and the lot fell upon Levi, for the number ten was the number which fell. And on the second counting Levi came out tenth.

**32:8** And Jacob rose in the night and sanctified Levi and put clean garments upon him and anointed him with the holy oil.

**32:9** And on that night, at the gate of Bethel, Jacob counted ten of all his cattle for the LORD, and he set them apart; and they were the tithe.

**32:10** And in the morning he called his son Levi and read to him all the things that had been appointed for the priests, and he commanded him to minister before the LORD, and to do all things as he had commanded.

**32:11** And the LORD appeared to Jacob at Bethel again, and blessed him and said: "Thy name shall no more be called Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name."

**32:12** And he said to him: "I am the LORD thy God who created the heavens and the earth. I will multiply thee and make thee fruitful, and kings shall come forth from thee, and they shall rule over all mankind."

**32:13** "And I will give to thy seed all the land under heaven, and they shall rule over all the nations according to their desires, and afterwards they shall take the whole earth."

**32:14** And he finished speaking with him, and went up from him. And Jacob looked till he ascended into heaven.

**32:15** And he saw in his vision of the night, and behold an angel came down from heaven with seven tablets in his hands. And he gave them to Jacob, and Jacob read them and knew all that was written therein which would befall him and his sons throughout all the ages.

**32:16** And Jacob showed the tablets to his father Isaac that night at Bethel. And his father read them and wept, and said: "All these things will indeed come upon thy seed in the future generations."

**32:17** And Isaac rejoiced concerning Jacob, because Jacob's seed would be established as great. And he blessed his son on that night and slept.

**32:18** And Jacob went to Rachel, and Rachel had conceived and was with child. And Jacob wrote all of these things in a book.

**32:19** And in those days the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, rose up against Jacob and his children.

**32:20** But they did not prevail against Jacob because the LORD had spread the fear and the dread of Jacob over all the nations and the peoples around about him. And he gave him glory, and they did not harm him.

**32:21** And Jacob's father-in-law Laban died that year. And the sons of Jacob were twelve in number.

**32:22** And Rachel bore a second son, and Jacob called his name Benjamin, the son of the days — that is, the son of his old age.

---

*EMET notes: The priestly investment of Levi (vv.4-10) in Jubilees is a key passage: Levi is designated by lot from among Jacob's sons, and the tenth lot falls to him, establishing the tithe-priest connection. The seven tablets vision (vv.15-16) is a Jubilees-specific motif. "Son of the days" for Benjamin is a literal rendering of the Ge'ez etymology.*
